paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. David had a plan, a whole nation behind him, and a parade of harps, cymbals and trumpets, and he opened by asking, "If it seems good to you, and if this is of the LORD our God" (1 Chronicles 13:2). All that joy was real. Even so, this day shows that God is not to be handled casually, because "the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah" and he died "because he had put his hand on the ark" (1 Chronicles 13:10).

I think this one hurts, and I won't pretend it doesn't. David got angry, and then the text says, "That day David feared God" (1 Chronicles 13:11-12). He didn't shrug it off, and he didn't bulldoze ahead with the plan. He stopped and asked, "How can I ever bring the ark of God to me?" (1 Chronicles 13:12). If that had been me on my gold base, I'd have been spinning in circles, so the stopping and the asking stand out to me.

Then look where the ark goes. David took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, and "the LORD blessed his household and everything he owned" (1 Chronicles 13:14). So hear both halves, baker: God is holy and worth taking seriously, and God also blesses. Hold onto that, because this story isn't over yet.
